answer.rationale: Finance has mandated an 18% spend cut and the incumbent has refused to reopen price this cycle (memory_c4 confirms renegotiation works, but only when the other side is willing to move). The primary contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renew, so deferring (memory_c5) would push us past the deadline into a month-to-month gap with a vendor who is already refusing price concessions. The low-cost vendor's quote alone meets the mandate, and memory_c2 directly attests that moving primary supply to this vendor cut unit cost sharply, onboarding was quick, and invoicing remained accurate — this is the strongest evidence on the table for the primary objective (minimize TCO) and I want to verify it before committing to switching the primary supply line. The 94% volume with no buffer (memory_c3) makes single-sourcing risky on its own, but I have capacity for exactly one decision this cycle and the contract clock is the binding constraint; the low-cost vendor's prior accuracy and stability record is what makes switching — rather than deferring or negotiating further with a party that has already said no — the right move now. Multi-year commitments (memory_c6) and renegotiation leverage (memory_c4) remain available levers in future cycles once this transition is locked in.
